11.text:
The verse opens with the address and the command in one breath: "O believers! Remember Allah's favour upon you". What follows names that favour in a single event, "when a people sought to harm you, but He held their hands back from you", and the two halves belong together, because the harm was intended and the hands that would have carried it out were held. The verse does not describe the plan or count the enemies; it names the outcome, which is the part the believers are meant to remember, and the memory is the reason the community is still standing on the day the words reach it. The reminder then becomes a command, "Be mindful of Allah", and that command puts the whole event under the fear of the One who held the hands back, so that what is remembered is not the good fortune of a people but a favour owed to the One who gave it. Then comes the sentence that answers the fear with trust: "And in Allah let the believers put their trust". A people who have just been reminded how near the harm came are told where their reliance belongs, and the order of the two sentences is the point of the verse, since trust follows the memory of the rescue and does not come before it. The verses before this one named the covenant taken from the Children of Israel and the justice the believers owe one another and their enemies; this verse shows the same favour reaching the community of the sūrah in the plainest shape of a plot that did not succeed. It also stands as the ground of what follows, because the verses after it turn to the People of the Book and to what they have hidden of the Scripture, and a community reminded of its own rescue is a community that will be asked to carry the light that has come. The verse is short, and its shortness is the shape of the thing it describes: a danger that came close, a hand that held it back, and a trust that has somewhere to rest.

**The justice this passage asks of the believers.**

There are usually two causes which hold people back from doing justice and then make them do the unjust and the oppressive. When it comes to doing justice, let nothing affect you, neither your own self, nor your parents, nor your relatives. The essence of this verse from Surah al-Ma'idah is that hostility against an enemy should not affect your sense of justice to the limit that you start working against the demands of justice to harm your enemy. This is the reason why, by placing 'al-qist' (justice) first in the verse of the Surah al-Nisa', it was said: ... be upholders of justice, witnesses for Allah ...) and, by placing 'lillah' (for Allah) first in the verse of Surah al-Ma'idah, it was said: ... be steadfast for Allah as witnesses for justice) - though, both these modes serve the same purpose end-wise. It is obvious that a person who stands for justice will stand for none but Allah, and one who stands for none but Allah will do nothing but justice. But, when it comes to protecting personal interest or favouring friends and relatives, one may be tempted to justify the thought that the act of caring for relationships here is also for Allah. Therefore, by bringing in the word, 'al-qist' (justice) first at that point, the message given was that the concession which is contrary to justice cannot be for Allah. And in Surah al-Ma'idah, where the purpose was to enjoin justice with enemies, the word 'lillah' (for Allah) was brought in first, which took away the chances of sentimental attachments overpowering human nature. The point is, when you stand for Allah, the inevitable outcome should be an equal justice with enemies as well. The second instruction given in these two verses is that no one should avoid recording true evidence and stating what is the truth in honesty with Allah, so that the decision makers face no difficulty in arriving at the true, sound and just decision. The Holy Qur'an has stressed upon this subject in several verses with various angles telling people not to drag their feet and be tardy in appearing as true witnesses.

**The pledge and the reminder of Allah's favour.**

And remember Allah's favor to you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said: Verily, Allah is All-Knower of that which is in the breasts O you who believe! Stand out firmly for Allah as just witnesses; and let not the enmity and hatred of others make you avoid justice. Be just, that is nearer to Taqwa; and have Taqwa of Allah. Allah says that He knows the secrets and thoughts that the hearts conceal,. (O you who believe! Stand out firmly for Allah...) meaning, in truth for the sake of Allah, not for the sake of people or for fame,. It is recorded in the Two Sahihs that An-Nu'man bin Bashir said, "My father gave me a gift, but 'Amrah bint Rawahah, my mother, said that she would not agree to it unless he made Allah's Messenger as a witness to it. Allah reminds His believing servants of His bounty by legislating this glorious religion and sending them this honorable Messenger. This is the pledge that they used to give to the Messenger of Allah when they embraced Islam. It was also said that this Ayah reminds the Jews of the pledges and promises Allah took from them to follow Muhammad and adhere to his Law, as 'Ali bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas stated.

**The favour, and the hands that were held back.**

O you who believe remember God’s favour upon you when a people namely Quraysh purposed to extend their hands against you in order to attack you but He restrained their hands from you and protected you from what they intended to do to you; and fear God; and in God let the believers put their trust. Be mindful of Allah by fulfilling His instructions and avoiding His prohibitions. Let the believers place their reliance in Allah alone, in order to achieve their religious and worldly interests. Muhammad and his Companions (Remember Allah's favour unto you) recollect Allah's grace by driving away from you the harm of the enemy, (how a people) the people of the Banu Qurayzah (were minded to stretch out their hands against you) to kill you (but He withheld) He prevented (their hands from you) from killing you; (and keep your duty to Allah) fear Allah in relation to that which He has commanded you.

**The lesson for a community that leaves its pledge.**

A pledge was taken from the Children of Israel by their prophet that they would lead a godly life, and twelve chiefs from their twelve tribes were appointed to keep a watch over them. Ways of salvation which are supposed to lead a man to his destination without discharging the claims or rights of his fellowmen, are sought. In the name of the call for truth, meaningless worldly activities find favour with such communities. In other words, they concoct a religion of their own, keeping purely worldly considerations in view, and start calling it the religion of God. Once a group reaches this stage in its wrong-doing, God withdraws His attention from it. Deprived of Divine guidance, such people reach the stage where they understand only the language of their base desires and remain preoccupied with satisfying their desires, until the angel of death approaches in order to catch hold of them and take them to the court of God. But when the communities blessed with Divine Scriptures go astray, they turn to the right or left of this highway.

**The man with the sword, and the peace he was given.**

The man took the sword out of its scabbard, moved it about but whenever he was on the point of striking the Prophet with it, Allah, glorious and majestic is He, restrained him. The Bedouin repeated the same question two or three times, and the answer of the Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, was always the same: This man then proceeded to the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, and found him sitting with his sword in his lap.

12.text:
The verse turns to a covenant and to the people who were bound by it, and it begins with the act of God rather than the act of man: "Allah made a covenant with the Children of Israel and appointed twelve leaders from among them and then said". The leaders are named in the same breath as the covenant, and that order matters, because the promise was made to a people and then placed in the hands of men who would answer for it, and the twelve are the shape the covenant took among them. What is said next is the promise itself: "I am truly with you". The words are short because everything that follows rests on them, and the presence of God with a people is the whole of what a community can be given. Then the conditions are named in a run of clauses: "If you establish prayer, pay alms-tax, believe in My messengers, support them, and lend to Allah a good loan". The worship comes first, the alms follow, and the two are the pillars of the life of a community; then the messengers are named together with the duty of supporting them, so the faith of that people is not a private matter but a public one, and a good loan completes the list as the sign that their wealth is not their own. The reward is set beside the conditions and is greater than them: "I will certainly forgive your sins and admit you into Gardens under which rivers flow". Forgiveness answers what they have done and the Gardens answer what they lack, and the mention of the rivers gives the promise the shape of a place rather than an idea. The verse closes on the warning that has been the point of the passage: "And whoever among you disbelieves afterwards has truly strayed from the Right Way", which places the covenant behind the reader as a thing received and the way ahead as a thing to be kept. The verses before it took the pledge of the believers in the plainest terms and reminded them of the covenant that carries the name of God; this one shows that covenant in the history of a people who were given leaders, worship, wealth and messengers, and it shows what the loss of it looks like when the conditions are put aside. What follows turns at once to those who broke what they had accepted, so this verse stands as the promise and the next as the reckoning, and the reader is meant to hear both together.

**The occasion the passage remembers.**

This verse particularly mentions how enemies conspired to destroy Muslims and kill their Prophet on so many occasions, but Almighty Allah foiled all their plans and put them to disgrace - 'some people planned to lay their hands on you, and He kept their hands away from you.'. First of all, what is being said here is that this blessing from Allah is not restricted to the Holy Prophet rather, the real cause of this Divine support and protection is the quality of Taqwa (the fear of Allah) and Tawakkul (Trust in Him). Any nation, or individual who lives by these two virtues, in any time and in any place, will have the support and protection from Almighty Allah in the same manner. In the seventh verse of Surah al-Ma'idah which appeared earlier Allah Almighty has asked Muslims to remember the pledge taken from them to which they professed belief and obedience: And remember Allah's favour upon you and His Covenant that He has taken from you when you said, "We have listened and obeyed.

**The covenant and the twelve leaders.**

God had made a covenant with the Children of Israel for what will be mentioned shortly and We raised up there is a shift of address away from the third to the first person from among them twelve leaders from each tribe one leader to be responsible for his people’s fulfilment of the covenant as a way of binding them to it. Surely if la-in the lām is for oaths you establish the prayer and pay the alms and believe in My messengers and succour them help them and lend to God a goodly loan by expending in His way I will absolve you of your evil deeds and I will admit you to gardens underneath which rivers flow. So whoever of you disbelieves after that covenant surely he has strayed from the right way’ he has erred from the path to Paradise al-sawā’ originally means ‘the middle way’. Allah had taken a firm promise from the Children of Israel, when He appointed over them twelve chiefs who were placed in authority over them. I am with you- with my help and support if you establish the prayer in the complete manner, give Zakat from your wealth, accept all of my messengers without distinction, honour them, assist them and spend in good causes. If you do all of this, I will wipe out the sins you commit and I will enter you, on the Day of Judgement, into gardens with palaces overlooking flowing streams. Whoever disbelieves after making this promise has knowingly and deliberately deviated from the path of truth. (Allah made a covenant of old with the Children of Israel) the acknowledgement of the Children of Israel in the Torah of Muhammad, that they shall worship none except Allah and that they shall not ascribe partners to Him (and We raised among them twelve chieftains) 12 messengers; and it is said: 12 kings, a king to each tribe: (If you establish worship) if you establish the prayer which has been made obligatory upon you (and pay the poor-due) from your wealth, (and believe in) acknowledge and accept (My messengers) who are sent to you (and support them) and assist them with the sword against the enemy, (and lend unto Allah a kindly loan) genuinely from your heart, (surely I shall remit your sins) other than the enormities, (and surely I shall bring you into Gardens beneath which) beneath its trees and habitations (rivers) rivers of water, milk, wine and honey (flow. Whoso among you disbelieveth after this) after accepting and acknowledging the covenant (will go astray from a plain road) such a person has erred from the road of guidance.

**The pledges and the promises taken from them.**

So We planted amongst them enmity and hatred till the Day of Resurrection; and Allah will inform them of what they used to do. "I am with you if you perform the Salah and give the Zakah and believe in My Messengers; honor and assist them, and lend to Allah a good loan, verily, I will remit your sins and admit you to Gardens under which rivers flow (in Paradise). So, because of their breach of their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts grow hard. They changed the words from their (right) places and have abandoned a good part of the Message that was sent to them. And you will not cease to discover deceit in them, except a few of them. Verily, Allah loves the doers of good And from those who call themselves Christians, We took their covenant, but they have abandoned a good part of the Message that was sent to them. (and lend to Allah a good loan...) by spending in His cause, seeking to please Him. (verily, I will remit your sins) and errors, I will erase them, cover them, and will not punish you for them,. Allah commanded His believing servants to fullfil the promises and pledges that He took from them and which they gave His servant and Messenger, Muhammad, peace be upon him. Allah also commanded them to stand for the truth and give correct testimony. He also reminded them of the obvious and subtle favors of the truth and guidance that He granted them. Next, Allah informed them of the pledges and promises that He took from the People of the Book, who were before them, the Jews and Christians. When they broke these promises and covenants, Allah cursed them as a consequence and expelled them from His grace and mercy. He also sealed their hearts from receiving guidance and the religion of truth, beneficial knowledge and righteous actions. These twelve people were leaders who gave the pledge to Allah to listen and obey Allah, His Messenger and His Book on behalf of their tribes. Muhammad bin Ishaq and Ibn 'Abbas said that this occurred when Musa went to fight the mighty enemy (in Palestine), and Allah commanded him to choose a leader from every tribe. Ka'b bin Malik mentioned these men in his poem, as recorded by Ibn Ishaq.On that night, these men were the leaders or representatives of their tribes by the command of the Prophet .

**The community that broke its pledge.**

Ways of salvation which are supposed to lead a man to his destination without discharging the claims or rights of his fellowmen, are sought. In the name of the call for truth, meaningless worldly activities find favour with such communities. Once a group reaches this stage in its wrong-doing, God withdraws His attention from it. Deprived of Divine guidance, such people reach the stage where they understand only the language of their base desires and remain preoccupied with satisfying their desires, until the angel of death approaches in order to catch hold of them and take them to the court of God. The pledge taken from the Children of Israel was that they would make themselves godly by offering salat (prayers); that they would discharge the rights of others in the shape of zakat (obligatory alms-giving); align themselves on the side of God by supporting His prophets; and spend their assets in support of the struggle for the religion of God. It was only after undertaking all this and after establishing a collective system among themselves for ensuring the continued fulfillment of these duties that they were entitled to God’s company and support, and entitled to enter the aesthetic atmosphere of paradise, after being purified. One attains paradise by the performance of good deeds and not due to any racial relationship. This is the highway which leads all human beings towards God and His paradise. But when the communities blessed with Divine Scriptures go astray, they turn to the right or left of this highway. Now, it happens that with the help of self-made interpretations the concepts of religion are changed.

13.text:
This verse explains what followed the covenant that the passage has just described, and it opens on the cause: "But for breaking their covenant We condemned them and hardened their hearts". The two consequences stand together, the judgment that was pronounced on them and the hardening that settled inside them, and the second is the heavier of the two, because a heart that has grown hard no longer receives the correction that could have answered the first. The verse then names what they did with the Book they had been given: "They distorted the words of the Scripture and neglected a portion of what they had been commanded to uphold". 19.text:
The verse is addressed to the two communities that hold the earlier scriptures, and it begins with the call that the passage has used for them: "O People of the Book". What it announces is a coming that is placed in time: "Our Messenger has indeed come to you, making things clear to you after an interval between the messengers so you do not say, 'There has never come to us a deliverer of good news or a warner.'" The interval is named in the sources as the long period in which no prophet was sent, and it is the reason the coming is a mercy rather than a reproach, because a people left without a messenger for that length of time has an excuse that only a messenger can take away. The verse answers a defence before it is made, and it does so in the terms of the defence itself, so that the people can see that the two offices they say they never had have come to them together. The words of the defence are then turned around in the next sentence: "Now there has come to you a deliverer of good news and a warner". The good news and the warning are the two halves of the message, one for the people who answer it and one for those who refuse, and both of them are present in the messenger who has arrived. The verse closes on the ground of the sending: "And Allah is Most Capable of everything". The one who was able to send a messenger after the interval is able to hold the people to what the messenger brought, and the sentence leaves the reader with the account rather than with a dispute about the interval. The verses before it spoke of the light and the Book and of the guidance they bring; this one names the people who received the messenger and the long silence that came before him, so the passage has been building from the covenant to the Book and now to the messenger who explains it. What follows turns from the account to the behaviour of those who received it.

**The interval between the messengers.**

Obviously, the verse seems to indicate the fate of the group of people who were not visited by any messenger or prophet or their deputies, nor did they have the religious laws of past prophets preserved with them; such people will be considered excusable and will deserve no punishment on the condition that such people should have not committed Shirk, the grave sin of ascribing partners in the Divinity of Allah. Therefore, Muslim jurists differ about rulings which apply to the people of Fatrah , particularly about whether or not they will be forgiven. The majority tilts towards the hope that they will be forgiven if they had kept adhering to the religion which had survived with them as originating from Sayyidna Musa or Sayyidna 'Isa irrespective of its authenticity - again, subject to the condition that they had not been hostile to the principle of Tauhid, the Oneness of Allah, and had nothing to do with the practice of Shirk. A question may arise here that the Jews and Christians, the people of the Book, who are being addressed in this verse did have the Torah and the Evangel and their sages and scholars with them even if no messengers reached them during this gap. How then could they come up with the excuse on the Day of Judgment that they had received no guidance? When, by addressing the people of the Book in this verse, it was said that Our Messenger, Muhammad al-Mustafa has come after a long gap,' there emerges a subtle hint towards the need that people who have been honoured with his presence among them should consider this as a matchless blessing and a supreme asset because the line of prophets had remained suspended since a long time and it has been opened for them once again. In the backdrop of a time such as this, the mission of reviving a people so lost was no easy task. This time was the notorious Jahiliyyah, commonly identified as the Age of Ignorance, and the people from it who were entrusted with the Prophet of Islam were spoiled, self-centered and uncompromising. Imagine the mission of a physician who treats a hopeless patient and does it at a place which lacks medical instruments, and medicines too, yet he succeeds in his effort to treat the patient to the limit that this patient, not simply that he rises from his death-bed to be-come a healthy person, but that he goes way ahead and himself turns into an expert physician and healer as well - if so, who can doubt the perfection of the master healer! The word, "fatrah" in: ‌ ‌ (after a gap between Messengers) literally means to slacken, to become dormant or to suspend or to terminate an activity. It signifies the suspension of the coming of prophets for a certain interval of time which is the period of time in between Sayyidna Isa and the Last of the Prophets, Sayyidna Muhammad al-Mustafa . According to Sayyidna Abdullah ibn Abbas there is a period of one thousand and seven hundred years between Sayyidna Musa and Sayyidna Isa .

**The long time without a messenger.**

"There came to us no bringer of glad tidings and no warner. Therefore, the Hadith states that Allah looked at the people of the earth and disliked them all, both the Arabs and non-Arabs among them, except a few among the Children of Israel, or a few among the People of the Book as Muslim recorded. The religion was distorted and changed for the people of the earth until Allah sent Muhammad , and Allah, thus, guided the creatures and took them away from the darkness to the light and placed them on a clear path and a glorious Law. Allah is addressing the People of the Book – the Jews and the Christians, saying that He has sent His Messenger Muhammad to them, the Final Prophet, after whom there will be no Prophet or Messenger. Rather, He is the Final Messenger who came after a long time passed between him and 'Isa, son of Maryam peace be upon them. There is a difference of opinion about the length of time between 'Isa and Muhammad . There is no contradiction here if we consider the fact that those who said that this period was six hundred years were talking about solar years, while the second refers to lunar years, since there is a difference of about three years between every one hundred lunar and solar years. (And they stayed in their Cave three hundred years, adding nine.)[18:25] meaning, nine more lunar years to substitute for the difference between lunar and solar years, thus agreeing with the three hundred years that the People of the Book knew about. We should assert again that the time period we mentioned here was between 'Isa, the last Prophet to the Children of Israel, and Muhammad , the Last Prophet and Messenger among the children of Adam. In the Sahih collected by Al-Bukhari, Abu Hurayrah said that the Messenger of Allah said,. This Hadith refutes the opinion of Al-Quda'i and others, that there was a Prophet after 'Isa called Khalid bin Sinan. Allah sent Muhammad after a period of time during which there was no Prophet, clear path, or unchanged religions. Therefore, the bounty of sending Muhammad was the perfect bounty at a time when he was needed the most.

**The bringer of good news and the warner.**

O People of the Scripture there has verily come to you Our Messenger Muhammad making clear to you the laws of religion after an interval between the messengers for there was no messenger between him and Jesus an interval of 569 years; lest you should say if you are punished ‘There has not come to us any bearer of good tidings min bashīr the min is extra nor any warner’. Indeed there has come to you a bearer of good tidings and a warner and so you shall have no excuse. God has power over all things including punishing you for not following him the Messenger. O People of the Scripture, Jews and Christians, My messenger Muhammad ﷺ has come to you after a period when there were no messengers and when there was a real need for his mission, so that you do not say as an excuse, ‘No messenger came to us bringing good news of Allah’s reward nor any warning of His punishment’. It is through My power that I sent the messengers and I sent Muhammad ﷺ as the final messenger. (O people of the Scripture!) O people of the Torah and the Gospel! (Now hath Our messenger) Muhammad ﷺ (come unto you to make things plain) that with which you have been commanded and that which you have been prohibited (after an interval) of cessation (of the messengers, lest ye should say) so that you will not say on the Day of Judgement: (There came not unto us a messenger of cheer) announcing Paradise (nor any warner) against hell.

**The warners and the bringers of good news.**

It is the way of God that He, on His behalf, raises certain individuals who acquaint the people with the realities of life; warn them of hell and give them the good news of paradise. It is only by supporting these ‘warners’ and ‘bringers of good news’ and cooperating with them that man finds God, and not in any other way.

20.text:
The verse turns back to Moses and to what he said to his people, and it opens with the command to remember the scene: "And remember when Moses said to his people". The words that follow are his own address to them, "O my people! Remember Allah's favours upon you when He raised prophets from among you", and they carry the affection of a leader who is about to remind a people of what they owe rather than to accuse them. The reminder itself is a list of favours, and the first of them is the one that is not wealth or land. The first of the favours is the one that is not wealth or land, A people given prophets from among themselves have been given a way to know what God wants of them, and the sources name this as the spiritual favour that stands above the rest. The second follows: "made you sovereign". The word carries a rule and a freedom, and the sources unfold it as the ending of the slavery of that people under Pharaoh and the giving of a position among the nations that they had not held before. The third is put in the widest terms of all: "and gave you what He had never given anyone in the world". What the earlier communities did not receive was given to them, and the verse puts it without naming the thing, so that the reader is left counting the gifts that his own life carries. The verses before this one answered the claims of the two communities about their standing with God; this one shows a prophet reaching the same lesson by another road, since the reminder of the gifts is the answer to the claim that a people have a standing of their own. What follows turns to what that people did with the favours they had been given, and the passage goes on from the remembrance of the blessings to the account that had to be given for them.

**The blessings Moses reminded his people of.**

Previous to the verses cited above, a pledge was mentioned in which the Bani Isra'il were bound to obey Allah and His Messenger. That event goes back to the time when Pharaoh and his army were drowned in the sea and Sayyidna Musa and his people, the Bani Isra'il, once delivered from the slavery of the Pharaoh, became the masters of Egypt. Then, to bless them with His added reward, and to let them repossess their ancestral land of Syria, Allah Ta ala commanded them through Sayyidna Musa that they should enter the Holy Land, that is, Syria, with the intention of Jihad. And along-with it, they were given the good news that victory will be all theirs in this Jihad - as Allah had made that holy land their destiny and they were bound to have it. They saw the blessings of Allah with their own eyes, they saw the spectacle of the drowning of Pharaoh and the conquest of Egypt, yet they failed, once again, to stand by the solemn pledges they had given and elected to sit out the Jihad of Syria squarely against this Divine command. Instead, they were free to move in an open area and actually travelled every day, right from the morning through the evening, with the intention of returning to Egypt, their homeland. But, when came the evening, they would find themselves exactly at the spot from where they had started in the morning. During this period, Sayyidna Musa and Sayyidna Harun left this mortal world and these people kept wandering in the wilderness of Tih. Thus, after the passage of full forty years, those who survived from among them resolved to take up the Jihad of Syria and Baytul-Maqdis under the leadership of the prophet of their time and the promise of Allah that the Holy Land had been destined for them was thus ful-filled. When Sayyidna Musa received the instruction to call his people to Jihad in order to conquer Baytul-Maqdis and Syria, he acted very much in accordance with his prophetic wisdom so crucial in giving good counsel. Therefore, before announcing the Divine command to his people, he reminded them of the many blessings bestowed upon them upto that time. The first of these is a spiritual blessing, that is, many prophets were sent to them continuously, a spiritual honour which can hardly be matched. It has been reported in Tafsir Mazhari that no other community has had such a large number of prophets as compared to Bani Isra'il. Hadith authority, Ibn Abi Hatim, reports on the basis of a narration from A'mash that in only one single period, the last period of the people of Bani Isra'il which extends from Sayyidna Musa to Sayyidna 'Isa one thousand prophets were sent to Ban' Isra'il. The second blessing mentioned in the verse quoted immediately above is a material blessing, that is, they were made masters and wielders of power. The hint given here is that the people of Bani' Isra'il who were the oppressed slaves of the Pharaoh and his people for many ages saw how Allah Ta ala destroyed their enemies and how they themselves were made masters and kings. (He made prophets from among you) which carries the sense that the whole people were not prophets, and this is the truth as prophets are only a few while the large body of people follows them. But, when it comes to the subject of temporal power on countries and states, said there was: (and made you kings) the outward sense of which is that they were made kings. Obviously, when a whole people cannot be all prophets, no people of a country can be all kings.

**The favours given to the Children of Israel.**

(and gave you what He had not given to any other among the nations ('Alamin).) means, during their time. (And indeed We gave the Children of Israel the Scripture, and the understanding of the Scripture and its laws, and the Prophethood; and provided them with good things, and preferred them above the nations (Al-'Alamin).)[45:16] Allah said,. Musa Reminds His People of Allah's Favors on Them; The Jews Refuse to Enter the Holy Land. (And (remember) when Musa said to his people: "O my people! Remember the favor of Allah to you, when He made Prophets among you,) for whenever a Prophet died, another rose among them, from the time of their father Ibrahim and thereafter. There were many Prophets among the Children of Israel calling to Allah and warning against His torment, until 'Isa was sent as the final Prophet from the Children of Israel. Allah then sent down the revelation to the Final Prophet and Messenger, Muhammad, the son of 'Abdullah, from the offspring of Isma'il, the son of Ibrahim, peace be upon them.

**The favours Moses named to his people.**

And mention when Moses said to his people ‘O my people remember God’s favour to you when He established among you that is from among you prophets and established you as kings possessing servants and retinues and gave you such as He had not given to any in all the worlds in the way of manna and quails the parting of the sea and other things. Remember, O Messenger, when Moses said to his people, the Israelites, ‘O People, remember, with your hearts and tongues, Allah’s favour to you when He made prophets amongst you calling you to guidance, made you kings in control of your affairs after you were subjugated slaves, and gave you such favours that He had not given to any other people in your time’. (And (remember) when Moses said unto his people: O my people! Remember Allah's favour) Allah's grace (unto you, how He placed among you) from you (Prophets, and He made you Kings) while you were slaves of Pharaoh before, (and gave you that (which) He gave not to any (other) of creatures) of your time in the wilderness: quails and honey.

**The group given a special position.**

It is the way of God that He chooses a group in order to convey His message to the people. Just as a particular person is the recipient of revelation, similarly a particular group is made the bearer of the revelation. In ancient times this special position was enjoyed by the Children of Israel and after the advent of the last of the prophets, his followers (ummah) were appointed to this position. Just as God requires of a community that it should represent His religion, similarly He also wants the community representing His religion to enjoy honours and high position in this world, so that it should be demonstrated to the people that in the new world coming into existence after Doomsday, prominence and distinction will be conferred only upon the ‘People of the Truth’.

21.text:
Moses turns from the reminder of the favours to the command that the favours were meant to lead to, and he addresses his people as his own: "O my people!". What he puts in front of them is a place and a promise: "Enter the Holy Land which Allah has destined for you to enter". The land is called holy because of what was placed in it rather than because of its people, and the sources name it as the land of Syria and Bayt al-Maqdis and the country around them. The command is not left without a warning, and the warning is about the step backwards rather than the enemy ahead: "And do not turn back or else you will become losers". The loss is put in the same word the sūrah has used for those who lose their own selves, so the verse makes the failure a matter of the will and not of the strength of the people who held the land. The same man who spoke these words had brought his people out of slavery and had seen the sea opened for them, and the sources recall the favours in that order so that the reader sees what was being asked of a people who had been given so much. The verses before this one showed Moses reminding his people of the favours of Allah; this one moves from the reminder to the demand, and the demand is the entering of the land that the favours had been preparing them for. What follows is the answer of the people, and it belongs with this verse because the answer shows what the warning had foreseen: a people told to go forward who decide that they cannot. The sources also note that the land had been assigned to that people in the promise given to their fathers, so the command was the taking up of something that had already been theirs, and the refusal was a refusal of the gift.

"Therefore it is forbidden to them for forty years; in distraction they will wander through the land. In it are a people of great strength, and we shall never enter it, till they leave it; when they leave, then we will enter. Two men of those who feared (Allah and) on whom Allah had bestowed His grace said: The Children of Israel were the most honorable among the people of their time, compared to the Greek, Copts and the rest of mankind. (which Allah has assigned to you) meaning, which Allah has promised to you by the words of your father Isra'il, that it is the inheritance of those among you who believe. (They said, "O Musa! We shall never enter it as long as they are there. So go, you and your Lord, and fight you two, we are sitting right here.") Compare this to the better response the Companions gave to the Messenger of Allah during the battle of Badr, when he asked for their advice about fighting the Quraysh army that came to protect the caravan led by Abu Sufyan. Several more Muhajirin also spoke, all the while the Messenger of Allah saying,. If you seek to cross this sea and went in it, we will follow you and none among us will remain behind. (And (remember) when Musa said to his people: "O my people! 36.text:
The verse turns from the call given to the believers to the state of those who refuse it: "As for the disbelievers". What is then placed before the reader is a measure of wealth beyond counting: "even if they were to possess everything in the world twice over and offer it all to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Judgment". Everything, and then everything again, and offered in full to buy back the self: the doubling is the figure that ends every figure, because there is no price left in this world that could stand in the place of faith. The answer is given without condition: "it would never be accepted from them". The ransom is refused, and the refusal is read as the plain statement that the day of judgment is not a market and that the wealth of the world has no weight in it; the gold of the earth, if a man brought its fill, would not be taken from his hand. What remains is named in one sentence: "And they will suffer a painful punishment". The word is left general, and the two halves are held together, a wealth that cannot buy and a punishment that will not lift. The verses before it commanded the believers to be mindful of Allah and to seek the way to Him; this one shows what the refusal of that way comes to, and the verse that follows goes on with the fire they will wish to leave but cannot.

**The ransom that will not be accepted.**

Have Taqwa of Allah and seek the Wasilah to Him, and strive hard in His cause, so that you may be successful Verily, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth, and as much again therewith to ransom themselves thereby from the torment on the Day of Resurrection, it would never be accepted of them. 38.text:
The verse names the offenders in the same shape, male and female together: "As for male and female thieves". The wording is taken as a deliberate pairing, so that the hand of the law falls on the thief and not on the man or the woman, and the crime is named while nothing turns on station or sex. What is prescribed is then stated in plain words: "cut off their hands for what they have done". The punishment is attached to the deed rather than to the person, and the hand is taken because it is the limb that did the taking; the conditions and the value are set out in full in the law, and the sentence is not carried out until they are met. The end of the sentence names what the punishment is for beyond the offender: "a deterrent from Allah". The word carries both the prevention of the offender and the warning to the people who see, and it is read as the reason the punishment is public, since the safety of the property of the whole community stands behind the sentence on one hand. The verse closes with the names that give it its ground: "And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise", the power that the law takes up and the wisdom that puts each penalty where it belongs. The verses before it opened the door of repentance to those who turn before they are seized; this one states the punishment of theft, and the verse that follows returns to the door and gives it to the thief who repents after his wrongdoing and mends what he has done.

**The hand of the thief and what is cut.**

And (as for) the male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands as a recompense for that which both committed, a punishment by way of example from Allah. This is also the view of Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal and Ishaq bin Rahwayh in one of the narrations from him, as well as Abu Thawr, and Dawud bin 'Ali Az-Zahari, may Allah have mercy upon them. (as a recompense for that which both committed, a punishment by way of example from Allah. And Allah is All-Powerful, All-Wise.) **The thief, male or female, and the hand.**

And the thieving male and the thieving female the definite article in both nouns relates to the subject sc. wa’lladhī saraqa wa’llatī saraqat ‘And the male who thieves and the female who thieves’; because this clause resembles a conditional statement sc. ‘if he thieves if she thieves’ etc. the fā’ has been included in the predicate fa’qta‘ū ‘then cut off’ cut off their hands that is the right hand of each of the two from the wristbone; it is explained in the Sunna that the amputation applies to the stealing of a quarter of a dinar and upwards and if the person were to re-offend the left foot should then be amputated from the ankle and then on subsequent re-offending the left hand is amputated followed by the right foot after which discretionary punishment is applied; as a requital jazā’an is in the accusative because it is a verbal noun for what they have earned and an exemplary punishment for both of them from God; God is Mighty His way will prevail Wise in His creation. (Allah is Mighty) in showing His anger towards the thief, (Wise) in that He decreed for him the cutting off of his hand.

39.text:
The verse that states the punishment of theft does not end the matter, and this one takes it back to the offender's own turning: "But whoever repents after their wrongdoing and mends their ways". The turn is not the word alone, and the pairing of repentance with mending is taken as the test: the wrongdoing is left and the life is set right, and a claim of sorrow that changes nothing is not the thing named here. What follows names the answer: "Allah will surely turn to them in forgiveness, Indeed". The turning is met by a turning, and the sentence is read as the ground of hope for the thief whose case never reached the court as well as for the one who stood under its sentence, with the rights of the people he wronged still owed by him. The verse closes on the two names that carry all of it: "Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful". Forgiveness for what is past and mercy for what is to come, and the pair is kept beside the punishment of the verse before so that neither side of the law is read alone. The verses before prescribed the cutting of the hand; this one gives the way back to the one who is sorry, and the verse that follows turns from the offenders altogether to the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and to the One who punishes and forgives as He wills.

**The forgiveness that follows the punishment.**

And whoever repents after his transgression and corrects himself, then Allah shall relent towards him. It will be recalled that forgiveness was also mentioned in connection with the Prescribed Punishment for robbery appearing a few verses earlier - and forgiveness has been mentioned after the punishment for theft as well. But, the statement of forgiveness at both places has a particular difference and it is on the basis of this difference that the sense of forgiveness in both punishments has been taken differently by Muslim jurists. While ordaining the punishment for robbery, giving an exception, Almighty Allah has said: ‌ (except those who repent before you overpower them - 5:34) the outcome of which is that the Hadd Punishment for robbery mentioned in the verse provides an exemption whereby the one who repents - before robbers are overpowered and arrested by the government - shall have his Hadd Punishment forgiven. As for the forgiveness mentioned after the punishment for theft, it does not have the exemption from this temporal punishment. In other words, the relevant ruler of the time will not abandon the Hadd Pun-ishment because of this repentance, instead of that, Almighty Allah will, by forgiving their crime, grant deliverance to them from the punishment of the Hereafter. But, should a thief were to forsake and repent from stealing after having committed a theft - whether before or after arrest - then, the Hadd of Sariqah, the Islamic Legal Punishment, which is a temporal punishment, will not be forgiven. However, if a criminal is truly repentant after committing a crime, seeks God’s pardon and completely refrains from such misdemeanours in future, then it may be hoped that God will forgive him in the Hereafter.

40.text:
The verse opens with a question put to the reader: "Do you not know that the kingdom of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah alone". What is named first is the ownership of all of it, and the question is taken as the ground of everything the passage before it has laid down, since the laws and the penalties and the forgiveness all belong to the One whose the kingdom is. The word alone stands in the same sentence to remove every partner from the rule. What follows describes the owner's freedom in His kingdom: "He punishes whoever He wills and forgives whoever He wills". The same will is named on both sides, and the sentence is read as the answer to anyone who would measure the punishments of the previous verses by his own sense of what fits, because the measure does not belong to the creature. Mercy and punishment are both placed in the hand that owns the heavens and the earth, and the two are set side by side so that neither despair nor presumption can take one of them alone. The question is put to the Prophet and through him to every reader, and it is asked of a people who have just been shown the penalties of the law and the open door of repentance beside them, so that the two are held together in the ownership that the sentence names. The verse closes with the name that carries both: "And Allah is Most Capable of everything". Capability over everything is the seal of the sentence, and nothing in what has been prescribed, no penalty and no forgiveness, lies outside the power that ordered it. The verses before spoke of the thief, the robbery and the war on the community, and of the door of repentance; this one lifts the reader to the ownership that stands behind every one of them, and it sets the tone for the passage that follows, where the Prophet is told what to do with the people who come to him for judgment.

**The punishments that are set for the crimes.**

But, in Hudud, if a testimony is not given immediately, instead of that, was given after one month or was delayed more than that, then, it will not be acceptable. It is to re-move this doubt that Almighty Allah has, in this verse, initially stated that He alone is the real Master of the entire universe. In between, comes the statement that it is not only that He punishes. He forgives as well, and that forgiveness and punishment depend on His Wisdom, for the way He is the Absolute Master and the Absolute Power, so is He Absolutely Wise too. There is no human power which can guage the extents of His mastery and domain so shall there be no human reason which can fully fathom the countless manifestations of His Wisdom - and that which it would pass on to human beings by virtue of pondering through principles is sufficient enough to put their hearts at peace. People in the West and those influenced by their education and culture commonly object that Islamic punishments are harsh. And as pointed out a little earlier, there are some heedless people who do not even hesitate to say that these punishments are savage and undignified. But, in the event that there be the necessary proof of crime available, the punishment given will be punitive (Ta'ziri). We know that the Holy Qur'an has it-self determined and fixed the punishments for only four crimes which are called Hadd, in the terminology of the Islamic Shari’ ah. The fifth Islamic Prescribed Punishment (Hadd) is that of drinking which is eighty lashes as fixed under the consensus of the Sahabah of the Holy Prophet . With the sole exception of these five crimes, the punishment of all other crimes has been left to the discretion of the ruler of the time so that the relevant judge may award the kind and amount of punishment with due consideration of the crime, the criminal and the circumstances. This is a matter in which it is also possible that some particular system de-signed to delimit and apportion punishments is established in consultation with those fit to guide and advise, and Qadis or judges are bound with it. Along with it, there is the standing rule of Islamic Law that the benefit of doubt goes to the person accused of a crime. This tells us that there will be many more situations in which the Hadd Punishment will not be enforced and, in their place, punitive punishments will be awarded subject to the discretion of the ruler of the time. Now the 'debate' is reduced to the punishments of five crimes only, and that too, in their particular situations. For example, let us take theft and see that the punishment of cutting the hand has not been imposed by the Shari ah on every theft, in an absolute sense - that is, theft as we know it in our common usage. For instance, the condition of a secured place tells us that property stolen from commonly used public places such as Masjid, masalla of Id (area earmarked for the large congregational prayers on the occasion of Idul-Fitr and Idul-Adha), Park, Club, Railroad Station, Waiting Room, Train, Airplane etc., or stealing fruits hanging on trees, or stealing honey will not cause the Hadd of Sariqah to be imposed against the thief, instead of that, punitive punishment will be given to the culprit as generally done in most countries.

**The least amount and the cutting of the hand.**

And (as for) the male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands as a recompense for that which both committed, a punishment by way of example from Allah. This Hadith is the basis of the matter since it specifies (that the least amount of theft that deserves cutting the hand) is a quarter of a Dinar. As for Imam Abu Hanifah and his students Abu Yusuf, Muhammad and Zufar, along with Sufyan Ath-Thawri, they said that the least amount of theft that deserves cutting off the hand is ten Dirhams, whereas a Dinar was twelve Dirhams at that time. The first ruling is the correct one, that the least amount of theft is one forth of a Dinar or more. This meager amount was set as the limit for cutting the hand, so that the people would refrain from theft, and this is a wise decision to those who have sound comprehension. Therefore, it is fitting that the tool they used to steal the people's wealth be cut off as punishment from Allah for their error. In Islam, there are several conditions that must be met before this punishment is carried out, as we will come to know, Allah willing. There are other rulings that Islam upheld after modifying these rulings, such as that of blood money for example. " During that night, the Messenger of Allah stood up and gave a speech and praised Allah as He deserves to be praised. The punitive system in Islam for social crimes has been formulated keeping in view two special aspects—one is punishment for a man’s crime and the other is the deterrent effect of that punishment. First hand experience of this nearness at that time takes the shape of aesthetic heavenly realization.

**The will that punishes and the will that forgives.**

He chastises him for whom He wills chastisement for and forgives him for whom He wills forgiveness and God has power over all things including chastising and forgiving. He punishes whomever He wishes through His justice; and forgives whomever He wishes through His grace. (Knowest thou not) have you not been informed, O Muhammad, in the Qur'an (that Unto Allah belongeth the Sovereignty) the stores (of the heavens and the earth? He punisheth whom He will) whoever deserves to be punished, (and forgiveth whom He will) whoever deserves to be punished.
